title: Privilege Escalation Incident Runbook
description: SOC response guide for detected privilege escalation attempts on Linux and Windows endpoints.
containment_steps: Immediately lock the compromised user account: `passwd -l <username>` (Linux) or `Disable-ADAccount` (Windows)
Revoke any newly granted sudo/admin privileges: remove from sudoers or strip group membership
Kill all active sessions for the compromised account: `pkill -u <username>` or `query session` + `logoff`
Block the source IP at the host firewall if the escalation originated remotely
Preserve volatile memory: dump running processes and open file handles before any remediation
investigation_steps: Review auditd/Sysmon logs for the exact syscall or binary that triggered the escalation (execve, setuid, sudo)
Check `/etc/sudoers` and `sudoers.d/` for unauthorized entries added since last known-good state
On Windows: query Security Event Log for 4672 (Special Logon), 4673, 4728, 4732 around the incident timestamp
Identify parent process chain: how did the escalating process get spawned? Trace back to initial access
Search for SUID/SGID binaries added or modified: `find / -perm -4000 -type f -newer /tmp/baseline 2>/dev/null`
Check for new local administrator accounts, unexpected group membership changes, or SSH key injection
Review cron jobs, systemd timers, and Windows scheduled tasks for persistence mechanisms added post-escalation
Correlate with MISP for known CVE exploits matching the escalation binary (e.g., polkit, sudo CVE-2021-3156)
remediation_steps: Patch the exploited vulnerability (kernel, sudo, polkit, or application) to latest stable version
Remove unauthorized sudoers entries, SUID bits, and any backdoor accounts
Rotate all credentials for accounts that touched the escalated session
Re-audit all privileged group memberships (wheel, sudo, Domain Admins, local Administrators)
Re-deploy host from clean image if kernel-level exploit is confirmed or rootkit presence is suspected
Add detection rule for the specific technique used: Wazuh rule, Sigma rule, or auditd watch
Enable AppArmor or SELinux profiles on affected Linux systems; enable Credential Guard on Windows
Schedule a privileged access review across all endpoints within 24 hours

escalation_criteria.escalate_to_tier3: Kernel exploit confirmed, rootkit indicators, or domain-wide privilege escalation
escalation_criteria.notify_management: Domain Admin or root compromise on production systems
escalation_criteria.legal_hold: If escalation is part of an insider threat or external breach investigation
